{{Short description|Norwegian chemist (1931–2010)}}
'''Per Johannes Kolsaker''' (30 September 1931 – 30 June 2010) was a Norwegian chemist.

He was born in [[Narvik (town)|Narvik]] as a son of book printer Johannes Fridtjof Olsen (1898–1975) and Johanne Otelie Trondsen (1896–1988). He, and his family, changed their last name to Kolsaker in 1945. He [[examen artium|finished]] his secondary education in 1950, enrolled at the [[University of Oslo]] and graduated with the [[cand.real.]] degree in 1958. He also participated in the [[Independent Norwegian Brigade Group in Germany]] in 1952.<ref name=snl>{{cite encyclopedia|year=|title=Per Johannes Kolsaker|encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]]|editor=|publisher=Kunnskapsforlaget|first=Tor Ragnar|last=Weidling|location=Oslo|url=http://www.snl.no/Per_Johannes_Kolsaker|language=Norwegian|accessdate=28 April 2011}}</ref>

He became a [[research assistant]] in chemistry at the University of Oslo, then a lecturer in 1966 and professor from 1992 to his retirement in 2001. In between he worked for the [[Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation]] in Tanzania from 1982 to 1983, and as an [[organic chemistry]] professor at the [[University of Tromsø]] from 1983 to 1986.<ref name=snl/>

He was interested in sports, including bridge, chess, golf and orienteering, and chaired the orienteering club [[IL Tyrving]] for two periods. He died in June 2010.<ref name=snl/>
